segment.text: Through devices like smartphones, tablets, and computers, we connect with the world around using wireless communication technology. Your Ford vehicle lets you do the same! Having a connected vehicle means that, depending on how it is equipped, your Ford can communicate wirelessly with apps on your mobile device and with us, our partners, and our service providers. Check out the Technology section on Ford.ie to learn about these technologies, and you can find out what connectivity technology can be used, or is installed on your vehicle by consulting your owners' manual. All digital roads are open to you when you purchase a Ford connected vehicle.

segment.text: Activation of the modem in our vehicles provides a multitude of customer benefits, enabling you to take advantage of our full suite of connectivity features. Modem activation becomes even more powerful when you connect your Ford with your phone, connecting your vehicle to eliglble Connected Services including complimentary trial periods. See Ford app Terms for details. Our equipped modem allows communication with the secure Ford cloud through cellular technology, much like a mobile device with a SIM card. Just like other parts of your vehicle, the cellular modem and its SIM are fitted at the factory. Many different technologies work together to provide the convenience and latest-available content that comes with staying connected. Internet service providers or mobile network operators play a huge part in enabling much of the wireless communication we rely on. Our equipped modem is no exception and we work with Vodafone as our network provider for the cellular data network on which Ford app remote features and most Connected Services rely. Once connected, your vehicle will send periodic alerts to us. These alerts contain a unique number which identifies your vehicle's SIM, your vehicle's VIN, and the electronic serial number of its modem. Just like in a mobile cellular device/mobile phone, these alerts enable you to have a fast and seamless experience when you're ready to connect your vehicle using the Ford app. Modem activation allows Connected Vehicle Information (described in more detail below) to be sent to us from your vehicle, and enables Ford Motor Company to conduct over-the-air software updates to the vehicle's software and systems. At the time of purchase of your new connected Ford, your dealer will explain to you how your vehicle gets fully connected and how you can take advantage of all that connectivity has to offer. When you take delivery, the dealer will ensure that your vehicle connectivity settings are customized to your preferences and tell you how to de-activate the connection if you choose. However connected you want to be, your SYNC system keeps you in control. You can set your preferences in vehicle, including in relation to what Connected Vehicle Information is shared with us, under Connectivity settings at any time. You can find out more about in-vehicle controls in your owners' manual. Please note that disconnecting the vehicle, or making changes to data sharing settings may impact the quality or availability of certain Connected Services. Because the vehicle will store your connectivity preferences and any data you import, like your address book, and may have associated Ford accounts, please don't forget to do a Master Reset if you ever sell your car, or buy a used vehicle equipped with a modem! Your owners' manual explains how to do this.

segment.text: There are some things you can look for in your car if you're wondering about its connectivity settings. You can check the status bar on the screen your in-vehicle infotainment system for alerts and notifications, including strength of nearby Wi-Fi networks or the strength of the connection coming from your mobile device. In certain vehicles you will see icons displayed which indicate that Connected Vehicle Information, which may include location, is being transmitted by the vehicle. For example, if your vehicle is fitted with FordPass Connect and a SYNC system with in-vehicle SYNC screen: alt Shows that the modem is activated and that Connected Vehicle Information excluding location is being transmitted. alt Shows that the vehicle's location is being transmitted. alt Shows the modem is activated, and that both Connected Vehicle Information and the vehicle's location are being transmitted. Not every situation is the same, so be sure to know how your vehicle is equipped. You can find out what connectivity equipment is installed in your vehicle, and how to tell what data is being transmitted from your vehicle, in your owners' manual or ask your dealer. You can also find out how to disconnect your vehicle in your owners' manual. Please note that disconnecting the vehicle, or changing data sharing settings, may impact the quality or availability of certain services.

segment.text: Ford has a connected vehicle cyber security team, and puts in place various technical and organizational security measures to protect Connected Vehicle Information, including access controls to limit unnecessary or unauthorized access to Connected Vehicle Information, as well as cyber security measures such as hashing and encrypting data. We actively participate in several joint industry forums focused on how to approach these complicated technical issues. In addition to mobile vehicle security professionals, we also work with organizations within the larger community of cybersecurity professionals, including the BITS Information Systems Audit and Control and Manufacturing work group, and apply these broader best practices to the vehicle, where applicable. Ford is also proud to be a founding participant in an industry-wide effort to address emerging issues through the Automotive Information Sharing Analysis Center (the Auto-ISAC ). The Auto ISAC serves as a central point for automakers, suppliers and other stakeholders to share cyber intelligence, coordinate, and respond to vehicle electronic cyber threats.
